What I'm imagining is a simple system where you can go to a subscribed verses tab, and then drag them up/down in a list based on which verses you want to see the most content from.I've been exploring the site a little,but I haven't noticed if this is already a feature. It would be a nice little feature to help this site stand out from Reddit, anyway.
Create an Option to Rank Subscribed Sub-verses, and Show Different Amounts of Content Based on That Ranking.

Instead of list dragging, what about numbering by importance? That way people who want to see all of them equally can just make them all set to "1" or something. Or have five 1s and a few 2s with just a couple 3s.
This is a much better way of doing it. You could create a generic 1-5 system that allows you to repeat the numbers if you want to see the same amount of content from a vers.

I like this idea because it reminds me of my music library I manage with MusicBee, in which I rate my entire library based on a five-star ranking, then have the player play more songs that are higher ranked.

But, I see a potential problem: how can we simplify such a system that most users can utilize it? I think many users may find it a waste of time if they need to organize a list just to use a feature. Perhaps, instead of a ranked list system, we could enable 'starring' a subverse, favoriting, so that more content will be displayed from starred subverses. Or, maybe an opt-in option to prioritize posts in your feed based on how many upvotes you gave in each respective subverse. But that may not be viable, since you'd generally have more upvotes in subverses you've subscribed to the most, so new subverses could be perpetually hidden indefinitely.

The other problem is reincarnating YouTube's sorting system, only giving you most of the videos from your subscriptions, so you'd miss out on some videos. Perhaps, instead of hiding content, it is instead sorted based off of the ranking, kind of how new posts are given a boost in the 'hot' feed.
